conflicts.description: The Bellwright Guild and the Cartographers' Circle each hold half of the knowledge needed to repair the skybridges, and neither will share it first.
conflicts.name: Secrets Versus Survival

conflicts.description: The Mist Riders argue the islands should let go of the failing skybridges and find new currents, while the other enclaves insist on mending them at any cost.
conflicts.name: Drift or Mend

description: Veyra is a fractured realm of four great floating islands, each tethered to the others by ancient skybridges: spans of living crystal and woven starlight raised in a forgotten age. For generations the bridges have carried trade, pilgrims, and shared weather currents, keeping the archipelago aligned in a single stable orbit around the Heartwind. Now the skybridges are dimming and cracking, and the islands have begun to drift apart. This is a wondrous high fantasy world for young adult readers, full of luminous cloud-seas, glider-borne messengers, living maps, and the awe of standing on a span of light above an endless sky. Magic here is rooted in resonance, meaning song, tuned metal, and chalk-drawn sigils. Craft, not explosive weaponry, shapes its tools and its wars. Rival enclaves guard their own secrets and distrust one another. A young cartographer must chart the failing bridges, uncover why they are dying, and persuade the islands to cooperate before the archipelago scatters into the void.

factions.description: Keepers of Lanternreach's archives, who believe accurate maps can map a path to saving the skybridges. Some members secretly suppress records that would embarrass the Circle.
factions.name: The Cartographers' Circle

factions.description: Ironmoor's master smiths, who tune the resonance bells that reinforce the skybridges. They sell their services dearly and keep their methods secret.
factions.name: The Bellwright Guild

factions.description: Glider-borne wanderers of Mistwild who say the bridges are failing because the islands have forgotten how to listen to the Heartwind. They favor letting the islands drift to new currents.
factions.name: The Mist Riders

history.description: The first skybridges were raised across the sky, joining four drifting islands into a single archipelago.
The Bellwright Guild withheld its bell-tuning secrets from Lanternreach, beginning centuries of distrust.
The Mistwild span fell silent for a full season, and the Mist Riders were blamed and shunned.
The first visible crack appeared in Heartspan, and the Cartographers' Circle quietly sealed the record of it.

locations.description: The central skybridge hub, a vast crystalline junction where all four main skybridges meet. Its resonance chambers hum with the pulse of the Heartwind, and it is the first place where cracks have appeared.
locations.name: Heartspan

locations.description: A terraced island of cartographers, lamplighters, and archivists. Its libraries hold the oldest maps of the skybridges, many of them incomplete or deliberately altered.
locations.name: Lanternreach

locations.description: A rugged island of tuned-metal foundries and wind-forges. Its smiths make resonance bells and bridge anchors, and they hoard their craft behind guild oaths.
locations.name: Ironmoor

locations.description: A cloud-drenched island of floating forests and glider-riders. Its people read the Heartwind in the mist and distrust the engineered order of the other enclaves.
locations.name: Mistwild

name: The Drifting Archipelago of Veyra

rules.statement: Each skybridge is held in place by a standing resonance between the islands it joins. When the tone weakens, the span loses cohesion and the islands drift.
The Heartwind flows through Heartspan and keeps the islands aloft. An island that drifts too far from it slowly sinks.
Volatile blast powders do not function in Veyra's resonant air, so all tools and weapons rely on tuned metal, tension, and sigil craft.
Chalk-drawn sigils sung at the right pitch can briefly stabilize a crack in a skybridge, but they fade by dawn.
Crossing a skybridge requires a toll token, and each enclave controls the tokens issued at its end of the span.
